title: Fixture Registry and Boundary Conditions
negative_results: A fixture-induced modal shift is classified as a FIXTURE_EFFECT (a known ordinary effect), never a specimen signal; refuse_fixture_effect_as_signal always raises.

A specimen id cannot be used where a fixture id is required, and a fixture id cannot be used where a specimen id is required; a specimen-shaped id is refused at record construction and in the mount specimen slot.

A fixture with an unrecorded preload cannot support a precision claim: assert_precision_claim raises BLOCKED_MISSING_INPUT because the contact stiffness and hence the modal frequency are unconstrained.
A boundary change is booked through the R13 energy ledger as ordinary boundary work; the ledger closes with residual_is_new_energy = false, so a fixture shift is never a new energy channel.
No fixture, specimen, mount, or measurement exists: every record is a SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE and every frequency is a declared model number in the R11 chain's own units.
reopening_test: Re-run `pytest tests/v8/test_fixtures.py -q`. Reopen P06 if any record in FIXTURE_REGISTRY stops conforming to fixture_record.schema.json, if fixture_shift_is_ordinary stops classifying a boundary-change shift as FIXTURE_EFFECT, if refuse_fixture_effect_as_signal stops raising, if a specimen id becomes usable as a fixture id (or vice versa), if a missing preload stops blocking a precision claim, or if a remount stops producing a distinct binding hash.

claims.statement: The fixture registry, boundary-condition modal model, error-budget contribution, run bindings, and reversal/permutation plans are software artifacts over declared model values.
A modal shift produced by changing the fixture boundary condition is a known ordinary effect, one of the explanations a residual must survive, and is refused as a specimen signal.

privacy_check: CLEAN - synthetic fixtures only, no private inputs
